summary.text: Karl Brabenec is a Republican member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 98, in Orange and Rockland counties, since his election in November 2014 and is running for re-election on the Republican and Conservative lines.
He previously served as Deerpark town supervisor.

paragraphs.text: Karl Brabenec is the son of Czech refugees and was raised in Orange County, graduating from Minisink Valley High School in 1997.
He earned a B.A. at Mount Saint Mary College and an M.P.A. from the John Jay College of Criminal Justice.
Brabenec worked as an assistant to former Orange County Executive Edward A. Diana, served on the Deerpark Zoning Board of Appeals, and served on the Deerpark Town Board from 2008 to 2010.
He was Deerpark town supervisor from 2010 to 2014.
Brabenec was elected to the Assembly on November 4, 2014; his district includes parts of Orange and Rockland counties, among them Deerpark, Port Jervis, Warwick, Monroe and Ramapo.
His official biography describes him as a former minority whip and former ranking member of the Labor Committee, and he serves on the Election Law, Labor and Rules committees.
It also says he lives in Westbrookville and has two children.
